questions.stem: A car travels at a speed of \(60\) km/h. If its speed is increased by \(20\)%, what will be its new speed?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(60\) km/h
Increase = \(20\)% of \(60\) = \(\frac{20}{100} \times 60 = 12\) km/h
New speed = \(60 + 12 = 72\) km/h

questions.stem: A train covers a distance in \(5\) hours at a speed of \(80\) km/h. If the speed is decreased by \(10\)%, how much time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Distance = \(80 \times 5 = 400\) km
New speed = \(80 - 10\)% of \(80 = 80 - 8 = 72\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{400}{72} = 5.56\) hours

questions.stem: A cyclist travels \(60\) km in \(3\) hours. If the speed is increased by \(25\)%, how long will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(\frac{60}{3} = 20\) km/h
New speed = \(20 + 25\)% of \(20 = 20 + 5 = 25\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{60}{25} = 2.4\) hours

questions.stem: Walking at \(\frac{6}{5}\) of his usual speed, a man reaches his destination \(10\) minutes early. What is his usual time to cover the distance?
questions.keySolution:
Let usual time = \(t\) minutes
New speed = \(\frac{6}{5}\) of usual speed
New time = \(\frac{5}{6}t\)
Given: \(t - \frac{5}{6}t = 10\)
\(\frac{t}{6} = 10\)
\(t = 60\) minutes

questions.stem: A vehicle travels \(150\) km in \(3\) hours, then \(200\) km in \(4\) hours. Find the average speed for the entire journey.
questions.keySolution:
Total distance = \(150 + 200 = 350\) km
Total time = \(3 + 4 = 7\) hours
Average speed = \(\frac{350}{7} = 50\) km/h

questions.stem: A person increases his speed by \(50\)% and reduces his travel time by what percentage?
questions.keySolution:
Let original speed = \(s\), time = \(t\)
New speed = \(1.5s\)
New time = \(\frac{t}{1.5} = \frac{2t}{3}\)
Reduction in time = \(t - \frac{2t}{3} = \frac{t}{3}\)
Percentage reduction = \(\frac{t/3}{t} \times 100 = 33.33\)%

questions.stem: A train \(200\) m long crosses a platform \(300\) m long in \(25\) seconds. If the speed is increased by \(20\)%, in how much time will it cross the same platform?
questions.keySolution:
Total distance = \(200 + 300 = 500\) m
Original speed = \(\frac{500}{25} = 20\) m/s
New speed = \(20 + 20\)% of \(20 = 24\) m/s
New time = \(\frac{500}{24} = 20.83\) seconds

questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point. Car A travels at \(60\) km/h and Car B at \(80\) km/h. After \(2\) hours, Car A increases its speed by \(25\)%. What is the distance between them after \(4\) hours from start?
questions.keySolution:
Distance covered by B in \(4\) hours = \(80 \times 4 = 320\) km
Distance by A in first \(2\) hours = \(60 \times 2 = 120\) km
A's new speed = \(60 + 25\)% = \(75\) km/h
Distance by A in next \(2\) hours = \(75 \times 2 = 150\) km
Total distance by A = \(120 + 150 = 270\) km
Distance between them = \(320 - 270 = 50\) km

questions.stem: A boat travels downstream \(96\) km in \(6\) hours and upstream \(60\) km in \(6\) hours. If the speed of the boat is increased by \(20\)%, what will be its new speed in still water?
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(\frac{96}{6} = 16\) km/h
Upstream speed = \(\frac{60}{6} = 10\) km/h
Speed in still water = \(\frac{16 + 10}{2} = 13\) km/h
New speed = \(13 + 20\)% of \(13 = 13 + 2.6 = 15.6\) km/h

questions.stem: A man covers half the distance at \(40\) km/h and the remaining half at \(60\) km/h. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.keySolution:
Let total distance = \(2d\)
Time for first half = \(\frac{d}{40}\)
Time for second half = \(\frac{d}{60}\)
Total time = \(\frac{d}{40} + \frac{d}{60} = \frac{3d + 2d}{120} = \frac{5d}{120} = \frac{d}{24}\)
Average speed = \(\frac{2d}{d/24} = 48\) km/h

questions.stem: A cyclist covers \(30\) km in \(2\) hours \(30\) minutes. If he increases his speed by \(20\)%, how much time will he save to cover the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Original time = \(2.5\) hours = \(150\) minutes
Original speed = \(\frac{30}{2.5} = 12\) km/h
New speed = \(12 + 20\)% = \(14.4\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{30}{14.4} = 2.083\) hours = \(125\) minutes
Time saved = \(150 - 125 = 25\) minutes

questions.stem: Two trains of equal length cross each other in \(10\) seconds when running in opposite directions. If one train is \(25\)% faster than the other and the slower train runs at \(36\) km/h, find the length of each train.
questions.keySolution:
Speed of slower train = \(36\) km/h = \(10\) m/s
Speed of faster train = \(36 + 25\)% = \(45\) km/h = \(12.5\) m/s
Relative speed = \(10 + 12.5 = 22.5\) m/s
Total distance = \(2L\) (where L = length of each train)
\(2L = 22.5 \times 10 = 225\) m
\(L = 112.5\) m

questions.stem: A person walks from A to B at \(5\) km/h and returns from B to A at \(7\) km/h. What is the average speed for the round trip?
questions.keySolution:
Let distance from A to B = \(d\) km
Time from A to B = \(\frac{d}{5}\) hours
Time from B to A = \(\frac{d}{7}\) hours
Total time = \(\frac{d}{5} + \frac{d}{7} = \frac{7d + 5d}{35} = \frac{12d}{35}\)
Average speed = \(\frac{2d}{12d/35} = \frac{70}{12} = 5.83\) km/h

questions.stem: A train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly. In the first \(10\) seconds, it covers \(50\) m. If its acceleration is increased by \(60\)%, what distance will it cover in the first \(10\) seconds?
questions.keySolution:
Using \(s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2\), where \(u = 0\)
\(50 = \frac{1}{2}a(10)^2\)
\(a = 1\) m/s²
New acceleration = \(1 + 60\)% = \(1.6\) m/s²
New distance = \(\frac{1}{2} \times 1.6 \times 100 = 80\) m

questions.stem: A bus covers \(240\) km in \(4\) hours. Due to traffic, its speed decreases by \(25\)%. How much extra time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(\frac{240}{4} = 60\) km/h
New speed = \(60 - 25\)% = \(45\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{240}{45} = 5.33\) hours = \(5\) hours \(20\) minutes
Extra time = \(5\) hours \(20\) minutes - \(4\) hours = \(1\) hour \(20\) minutes

questions.stem: In a \(100\) m race, A beats B by \(10\) m and B beats C by \(5\) m. By what distance does A beat C in the same race?
questions.keySolution:
When A completes \(100\) m, B covers \(90\) m
When B covers \(100\) m, C covers \(95\) m
When B covers \(90\) m, C covers \(90 \times \frac{95}{100} = 85.5\) m
A beats C by \(100 - 85.5 = 14.5\) m

questions.stem: A man rows a boat \(18\) km downstream in \(2\) hours and \(12\) km upstream in \(3\) hours. If the rowing speed is increased by \(50\)%, what will be the new speed in still water?
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(\frac{18}{2} = 9\) km/h
Upstream speed = \(\frac{12}{3} = 4\) km/h
Speed in still water = \(\frac{9 + 4}{2} = 6.5\) km/h
Current speed = \(\frac{9 - 4}{2} = 2.5\) km/h
New rowing speed = \(6.5 + 50\)% = \(9.75\) km/h
New speed in still water = \(9.75 + 2.5 = 12.25\) km/h

questions.stem: A truck travels \(420\) km on \(60\) liters of fuel. If fuel efficiency decreases by \(15\)%, how much fuel will be needed for the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Original efficiency = \(\frac{420}{60} = 7\) km/liter
New efficiency = \(7 - 15\)% = \(7 - 1.05 = 5.95\) km/liter
Fuel needed = \(\frac{420}{5.95} = 70.6\) liters

questions.stem: Two cars start simultaneously from the same point in opposite directions. One travels at \(50\) km/h and the other at \(70\) km/h. After how much time will they be \(360\) km apart?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(50 + 70 = 120\) km/h
Time = \(\frac{360}{120} = 3\) hours

questions.stem: A train running at \(90\) km/h crosses a bridge \(500\) m long in \(30\) seconds. If the speed is reduced by \(10\)%, what will be the new crossing time?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(90\) km/h = \(25\) m/s
Length of train = Distance covered - Bridge length
Total distance = \(25 \times 30 = 750\) m
Train length = \(750 - 500 = 250\) m
New speed = \(90 - 10\)% = \(81\) km/h = \(22.5\) m/s
New time = \(\frac{750}{22.5} = 33.33\) seconds

questions.stem: A person covers \(\frac{1}{3}\) of a journey at \(20\) km/h, \(\frac{1}{3}\) at \(30\) km/h, and the remaining at \(60\) km/h. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let total distance = \(3d\)
Time for first part = \(\frac{d}{20}\)
Time for second part = \(\frac{d}{30}\)
Time for third part = \(\frac{d}{60}\)
Total time = \(\frac{d}{20} + \frac{d}{30} + \frac{d}{60} = \frac{3d + 2d + d}{60} = \frac{6d}{60} = \frac{d}{10}\)
Average speed = \(\frac{3d}{d/10} = 30\) km/h

questions.stem: A car completes a journey in \(8\) hours at \(75\) km/h. If the speed is increased by \(25\)%, how much time will be saved?
questions.keySolution:
Distance = \(75 \times 8 = 600\) km
New speed = \(75 + 25\)% = \(93.75\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{600}{93.75} = 6.4\) hours
Time saved = \(8 - 6.4 = 1.6\) hours

questions.stem: A train \(300\) m long is running at \(60\) km/h. In how much time will it cross a man running at \(6\) km/h in the same direction?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(60 - 6 = 54\) km/h = \(15\) m/s
Time = \(\frac{300}{15} = 20\) seconds

questions.stem: A motorist covers \(200\) km at \(50\) km/h and the next \(300\) km at \(75\) km/h. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first part = \(\frac{200}{50} = 4\) hours
Time for second part = \(\frac{300}{75} = 4\) hours
Total distance = \(200 + 300 = 500\) km
Total time = \(4 + 4 = 8\) hours
Average speed = \(\frac{500}{8} = 62.5\) km/h

questions.stem: A person walks at \(4\) km/h for the first half of the time and at \(6\) km/h for the second half. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Let total time = \(2t\)
Distance in first half = \(4t\)
Distance in second half = \(6t\)
Total distance = \(4t + 6t = 10t\)
Average speed = \(\frac{10t}{2t} = 5\) km/h

questions.stem: A cyclist starts at \(8\) AM and travels at \(20\) km/h. Another cyclist starts at \(10\) AM from the same point and travels at \(30\) km/h in the same direction. When will the second cyclist overtake the first?
questions.keySolution:
At \(10\) AM, first cyclist has covered \(20 \times 2 = 40\) km
Relative speed = \(30 - 20 = 10\) km/h
Time to overtake = \(\frac{40}{10} = 4\) hours after \(10\) AM
Overtaking time = \(10\) AM + \(4\) hours = \(2\) PM

questions.stem: A train leaves station A at \(9\) AM traveling at \(80\) km/h. Another train leaves the same station at \(11\) AM traveling at \(100\) km/h in the same direction. How far from station A will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
At \(11\) AM, first train has traveled \(80 \times 2 = 160\) km
Relative speed = \(100 - 80 = 20\) km/h
Time for second train to catch up = \(\frac{160}{20} = 8\) hours
Distance from A = \(100 \times 8 = 800\) km

questions.stem: A man can row \(7.5\) km/h in still water. If the river flows at \(2.5\) km/h, how long will it take him to row \(15\) km downstream and return?
questions.keySolution:
Downstream speed = \(7.5 + 2.5 = 10\) km/h
Upstream speed = \(7.5 - 2.5 = 5\) km/h
Time downstream = \(\frac{15}{10} = 1.5\) hours
Time upstream = \(\frac{15}{5} = 3\) hours
Total time = \(1.5 + 3 = 4.5\) hours

questions.stem: A car covers a certain distance at \(60\) km/h and returns at \(40\) km/h. If the total time taken is \(5\) hours, what is the one-way distance?
questions.keySolution:
Let distance = \(d\) km
Time for onward journey = \(\frac{d}{60}\)
Time for return journey = \(\frac{d}{40}\)
Total time: \(\frac{d}{60} + \frac{d}{40} = 5\)
\(\frac{2d + 3d}{120} = 5\)
\(\frac{5d}{120} = 5\)
\(d = 120\) km

questions.stem: Two trains start from stations \(300\) km apart and travel towards each other at \(70\) km/h and \(80\) km/h respectively. After how much time will they meet?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(70 + 80 = 150\) km/h
Time to meet = \(\frac{300}{150} = 2\) hours

questions.stem: A train passes a telegraph post in \(8\) seconds and a platform \(264\) m long in \(20\) seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.keySolution:
Let length of train = \(L\) m and speed = \(v\) m/s
From telegraph post: \(L = 8v\)
From platform: \(L + 264 = 20v\)
Substituting: \(8v + 264 = 20v\)
\(264 = 12v\)
\(v = 22\) m/s
\(L = 8 \times 22 = 176\) m

questions.stem: A person covers \(40\) km at \(10\) km/h, next \(40\) km at \(20\) km/h, and the last \(40\) km at \(30\) km/h. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
questions.keySolution:
Time for first part = \(\frac{40}{10} = 4\) hours
Time for second part = \(\frac{40}{20} = 2\) hours
Time for third part = \(\frac{40}{30} = 1.33\) hours
Total time = \(4 + 2 + 1.33 = 7.33\) hours
Total distance = \(120\) km
Average speed = \(\frac{120}{7.33} = 16.36\) km/h

questions.stem: A policeman spots a thief from a distance of \(200\) m. When the policeman starts chasing, the thief also starts running. If the policeman runs at \(12\) km/h and the thief at \(10\) km/h, after how much time will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.keySolution:
Relative speed = \(12 - 10 = 2\) km/h = \(\frac{2 \times 1000}{3600}\) m/s = \(\frac{5}{9}\) m/s
Time = \(\frac{200}{5/9} = \frac{200 \times 9}{5} = 360\) seconds = \(6\) minutes

questions.stem: A man rows upstream \(16\) km in \(4\) hours and downstream \(24\) km in \(3\) hours. What is his speed in still water?
questions.keySolution:
Upstream speed = \(\frac{16}{4} = 4\) km/h
Downstream speed = \(\frac{24}{3} = 8\) km/h
Speed in still water = \(\frac{4 + 8}{2} = 6\) km/h

questions.stem: A train travels \(360\) km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been \(5\) km/h more, it would have taken \(1\) hour less. Find the original speed.
questions.keySolution:
Let original speed = \(v\) km/h
Original time = \(\frac{360}{v}\)
New time = \(\frac{360}{v+5}\)
Given: \(\frac{360}{v} - \frac{360}{v+5} = 1\)
\(360[\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{v+5}] = 1\)
\(360 \times \frac{5}{v(v+5)} = 1\)
\(1800 = v(v+5)\)
\(v^2 + 5v - 1800 = 0\)
Solving: \(v = 40\) km/h

questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point at the same time. One travels north at \(60\) km/h and the other travels east at \(80\) km/h. What is the distance between them after \(3\) hours?
questions.keySolution:
Distance traveled north = \(60 \times 3 = 180\) km
Distance traveled east = \(80 \times 3 = 240\) km
Distance between them = \(\sqrt{180^2 + 240^2} = \sqrt{32400 + 57600} = \sqrt{90000} = 300\) km

questions.stem: A bus normally covers \(450\) km in \(9\) hours. Due to bad weather, its speed is reduced by \(20\)%. How much extra time will it take?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(\frac{450}{9} = 50\) km/h
New speed = \(50 - 20\)% = \(40\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{450}{40} = 11.25\) hours
Extra time = \(11.25 - 9 = 2.25\) hours

questions.stem: A cyclist covers \(75\) km in \(5\) hours against the wind and \(90\) km in \(3\) hours with the wind. What is his speed in still air?
questions.keySolution:
Speed against wind = \(\frac{75}{5} = 15\) km/h
Speed with wind = \(\frac{90}{3} = 30\) km/h
Speed in still air = \(\frac{15 + 30}{2} = 22.5\) km/h

questions.stem: A person walks \(4\) km/h for \(2\) hours, then \(6\) km/h for \(1\) hour, and finally \(8\) km/h for \(30\) minutes. What is the average speed?
questions.keySolution:
Distance in first part = \(4 \times 2 = 8\) km
Distance in second part = \(6 \times 1 = 6\) km
Distance in third part = \(8 \times 0.5 = 4\) km
Total distance = \(8 + 6 + 4 = 18\) km
Total time = \(2 + 1 + 0.5 = 3.5\) hours
Average speed = \(\frac{18}{3.5} = 5.43\) km/h

questions.stem: A train \(150\) m long crosses a \(250\) m platform in \(20\) seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.keySolution:
Total distance = \(150 + 250 = 400\) m
Time = \(20\) seconds
Speed = \(\frac{400}{20} = 20\) m/s = \(20 \times \frac{18}{5} = 72\) km/h

questions.stem: A motorboat goes \(30\) km upstream in \(3\) hours and \(28\) km downstream in \(2\) hours. What is the speed of the current?
questions.keySolution:
Upstream speed = \(\frac{30}{3} = 10\) km/h
Downstream speed = \(\frac{28}{2} = 14\) km/h
Speed of current = \(\frac{14 - 10}{2} = 2\) km/h

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths \(100\) m and \(150\) m are running in opposite directions at \(40\) km/h and \(50\) km/h respectively. In how much time will they cross each other?
questions.keySolution:
Total length = \(100 + 150 = 250\) m
Relative speed = \(40 + 50 = 90\) km/h = \(25\) m/s
Time = \(\frac{250}{25} = 10\) seconds

questions.stem: A person covers a distance in \(6\) hours at \(8\) km/h. If he wants to cover the same distance in \(4\) hours, by what percentage should he increase his speed?
questions.keySolution:
Distance = \(6 \times 8 = 48\) km
Required speed = \(\frac{48}{4} = 12\) km/h
Increase in speed = \(12 - 8 = 4\) km/h
Percentage increase = \(\frac{4}{8} \times 100 = 50\)%

questions.stem: A train covers \(300\) km in \(5\) hours. If it reduces its speed by \(15\)%, how much extra time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.keySolution:
Original speed = \(\frac{300}{5} = 60\) km/h
New speed = \(60 - 15\)% = \(51\) km/h
New time = \(\frac{300}{51} = 5.88\) hours
Extra time = \(5.88 - 5 = 0.88\) hours = \(53\) minutes
